args.message: module.py implements solve(data) per the user contract: per-operation checks run in the specified order (kind, amount, hold id, then available funds), release ignores amount, no input mutation, and empty ops returns zeros. Public tests pass 3/3 with the delivered module.py (sha256 9c47953f...). Those public tests cover only basic cases, so the error paths (invalid kind, bool or non-positive amounts, duplicate or unknown hold ids, insufficient funds) were verified by reading the code, not by test runs.
